what_its_for: This medicine is used together with a reduced-calorie diet and regular exercise to help adults and some teenagers (12 years and older) lose weight. It is prescribed for people who are obese or overweight and have a weight-related health problem such as high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or type 2 diabetes.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth once every morning, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or break it open. Do not take it in the evening or at night because it may make it hard to fall asleep. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Follow your doctor's instructions carefully about when to increase or change your dose.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks to find the dose that works best for you. The starting dose is typically one low-strength capsule (3.75 mg phentermine / 23 mg topiramate) taken once every morning for 14 days. Your doctor may then increase your dose based on how you respond and how well you tolerate it. The maximum dose is 15 mg phentermine / 92 mg topiramate once daily. Never take more than prescribed, and never stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose the following morning at your regular time. Do not double up or take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. Taking an extra dose can increase your risk of side effects.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine past its expiration date. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine — it can increase dizziness and may cause serious side effects. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you, because it may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or difficulty thinking clearly. Avoid becoming overheated or dehydrated, especially during hot weather or exercise, since this medicine can reduce your ability to sweat. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can cause serious birth defects. Women of childbearing age must use effective birth control while taking this medicine. Avoid suddenly stopping the medicine without your doctor's approval.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience any of the following: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, depression or mood changes, fast or pounding heartbeat, chest pain, shortness of breath, vision problems or eye pain (which could be signs of increased eye pressure), numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, confusion or trouble thinking, memory problems, persistent or severe headache, decreased sweating with a high fever, signs of kidney stones such as severe back or side pain or blood in your urine, swelling of the face or throat, or if you miss a menstrual period (possible sign of pregnancy). Also tell your doctor if you are not losing at least 3% of your body weight after 12 weeks on the full dose.
when_it_works: Some people may begin to notice weight loss within the first few weeks, but it may take several months to see the full benefit. Your doctor will check your progress regularly — usually at 12 weeks — to see if the medicine is working well enough for you. This medicine works best when combined with healthy eating habits and regular physical activity.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant. It can cause cleft lip and cleft palate and other serious birth defects. A pregnancy test is required before starting treatment. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control throughout treatment and for one month after stopping. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine as it may pass into breast milk and harm the baby. Children: This medicine is approved for teenagers 12 years and older who are obese. It is not approved for children under 12. Older adults (65+): Use with caution. Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or may advise you not to use this medicine if you have moderate to severe kidney or liver disease. Glaucoma or hyperthyroidism: This medicine should NOT be used in people with these conditions.
